changes: A right sidebar with Overview, Agents, Skills and Workflows tabs. Overview shows what needs you, today's usage and the latest missions. Hide it to a slim icon rail (Ctrl+Alt+Shift+B, ⌘⌥B on Mac).

Copy from terminals: right-click for Copy, Paste, Select all and Copy all output. Ctrl+C copies when text is selected, and Ctrl+V pastes on Windows. In agent screens, hold Shift while dragging to select (Option on Mac).
Fix: Cursor missions failed on Windows. Cursor now starts as "agent" (or "cursor-agent" on older installs), and prompts arrive whole.
Fix: on Windows, a task that runs a .ps1 script opened it in Notepad. It now runs in PowerShell.

Fix: the app could freeze for a while, mostly on Windows. Token usage is now read incrementally, and tool lookups no longer block the app. If it still happens, About → Copy diagnostics lists each freeze.
GitHub Workflows splits into Workflows and Runs sections that scroll on their own, and workflow logs open on Windows too.
New shell tasks offer the scripts in their folder (package.json, Makefile, justfile, …) to pick from.
What's new: after an update, sldev-io shows what changed (also under Help → What's new, and on the website's changelog).
Report a bug or send an idea from the app: it opens a GitHub issue with your versions already filled in.
The taskbar and dock icon shows how many missions need you.
Optional sound when a mission needs you (Settings → General).
Fix: on Windows, agents received only part of the prompt (sometimes a single word). Agents now start without a shell, and every prompt arrives whole, with its line breaks, quotes and symbols.
Removing a mission asks first, says what is removed and kept, and never throws away uncommitted work unless you tick it. The same goes for every other delete.
Missions take acceptance criteria, keep the agent's final report, and take your handoff notes. Follow-up and Second opinion pass both on to the next agent.
Agents dashboard: every running agent with what it's doing, how long it has run and its tokens. Ctrl+Shift+J jumps to the next one that needs you.
Software Factory: recipes run agents and checks as a pipeline, with bake-offs, PR feedback and run history.
Agent profiles, rules sync to every agent's instruction file, and a usage dashboard with a timeline and estimated cost.
Missions, factory runs, skills and tasks can work in any folder: type a path, Browse…, or pick a recent one.
A new look: one colour per status everywhere, counts on the sidebar icons, start cards in the empty dock, Ping and Save & Connect for SSH hosts.
The version is shown in the title bar; click it to open Settings → About.
The terminal installer always installs the version from the website, even over a local build.
Automatic updates on Windows and Linux; on macOS the app tells you when a new version is out.
Settings → About with versions, diagnostics to copy and links to the legal pages.
The Linux build runs on older distributions (glibc 2.35 and newer).
Installers are published to the public downloads page.
The free beta runs until the date on the website.
First beta: terminals, runtimes and tasks, agent missions for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor Agent, GitHub Copilot, OpenCode, Gemini CLI and custom CLIs.
Skills, workflows, notes, SSH with a credential vault, Docker containers and a first-run setup check.
